public_rationale: The GPT-5 part holds. In October 2024 Altman said nothing OpenAI was working on for 2024 was worthy of the GPT-5 name (e1). The 'GPT-4 level with incremental changes' part is only half right. On general chat rankings, leading models were very close to each other in 2024 (e4). But OpenAI released o1 in September 2024 (preview) and December 2024 (full). On the 2024 AIME math exam it scored 74–83%, against 12% for GPT-4o (e2). That is a large jump, not an incremental one, on an ordinary reading. The post's caveat names only o3, which was announced but not yet released. It does not cover o1, which was already available. So one part of the claim holds and one is contradicted for reasoning-heavy tasks.
limitations: Whether o1's gains count as 'incremental' is a judgment; on general chat rankings o1 was not far ahead.
o1 was slower and costlier, which some would treat as a different product rather than a level jump.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Available AI models remain essentially GPT-4 level with incremental changes, and OpenAI has nothing it deems worthy of the GPT-5 label.

statement.excerpt: We are still basically surrounded by GPT-4 level models with incremental changes, and nothing that OpenAI themselves thinks is worthy of the GPT-5 label,
statement.document_title: 25 AI Predictions for 2025, from Marcus on AI

from_speaker: still basically surrounded by GPT-4 level models
nothing that OpenAI themselves thinks is worthy of the GPT-5 label
our_interpretation: Two parts. (a) Released models at the end of 2024 were roughly GPT-4 level, and the changes were incremental rather than large leaps. (b) OpenAI had not given any model the GPT-5 name and did not consider any of its 2024 work worthy of it.
He describes an ongoing state without naming a period. Since the post reviews 2024, the target period is calendar 2024 up to the post date.
His caveat covers only o3, which was announced but not released. Released models, including o1, fall inside the claim.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence shows released frontier models in 2024 were near GPT-4 with only modest gains, and OpenAI did not consider anything it had worthy of the GPT-5 label.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence shows a released 2024 model made large, non-incremental gains over GPT-4-class models, or that OpenAI released or endorsed a GPT-5-class model.
